title: fix(gateway): avoid setup failures during connection bursts
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes missing Control UI setup data and failed session creation when many users connect to one Gateway at once.

## User Impact

Concurrent setup requests can wait for their turn instead of receiving retryable server-busy errors. A single connection retains its previous waiting allowance; aggregate count, serialized bytes, control reserves, FIFO ordering, and yielding remain bounded. No configuration or protocol change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

A two-job Control UI bootstrap can run three approval-list RPCs and two cron RPCs together. At 100 clients that is 500 ordinary requests competing for only 256 waiting slots. A stall makes this easier to hit, but a fixed-clock owner regression reproduces the capacity mismatch without one.

The existing request-start owner now allows 1,024 ordinary waiting requests across connections and caps each connection at 256. It shares the existing control per-connection accounting instead of adding another scheduler. The 50 MiB ordinary byte limit and the separate 1,024-request/1 MiB control reserve are unchanged, as are 64 starts/12 ms yielding. This is bounded burst tolerance, not a CPU optimization or a fix for the remaining main-thread stalls.

Update/restart behavior: the request-entry owner still joins accepted preparation and rechecks closure and live authority after each queued start; this change adds no timeout, persistent state, or shutdown owner. The independent worker-drain shutdown fix is #162616; this PR is not stacked on it.

## Evidence

Same direct AWS c7a.8xlarge host, Gateway pinned to four cores and provider/drivers to the other 28. Frozen baseline `91e1bed6cdc6`, candidate `4c3246af34ea`; primary Node 26.9.0 and Bun fork `57fadf566d`. Exact synthetic provider streams, 100 protocol clients/50 active, real Control UI bootstrap contract, fresh isolated state.

| Actual 100-client connection burst | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Node authenticated handshakes | 100/100 | 100/100 |
| Node retryable setup refusals | 282 across 76 clients | **0** |
| Node completed exact replies | 50/50 | 50/50 |
| Bun authenticated handshakes | 100/100 | 100/100 |
| Bun retryable setup refusals | 226 across 65 clients | **0** |
| Bun completed exact replies | Setup aborted by refused session creation | **50/50** |

The Node setup ELD maximum remains **377.23 → 371.46 ms** while refusals disappear: this repairs bounded admission, not the independent setup stall. Bun baseline's 331 subsequent cleanup/closed-socket errors are not additional server refusals. Burst cells with missing setup work are excluded from normalized load comparisons.

Three matched 120-second steady controls before and after per runtime, with reversed pair order and a 60 ms connection stagger to separate setup refusal from load performance. All **12 controls are eligible**, with exact replies, verified build/runtime/affinity, and no integrity errors. The 17 reported control errors were post-drain `sessions.list` cleanup cancellations; none were setup refusals. These are medians of per-run metrics, not pooled percentiles; CPU covers load through drain.

| Runtime | Main CPU ms/reply | First delta p50 | First delta p95 | Load main CPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Node 26.9 | **522.14 → 503.04 (−3.66%)** | **14.297 → 13.283 s** | 17.876 → 17.196 s | 99.18% → 99.14% |
| Bun fork | **518.40 → 517.88 (−0.10%)** | **14.393 → 13.498 s** | **17.768 → 18.867 s (+6.18%)** | 98.53% → 98.45% |

**Bun tail parity remains unproven.** Its p95 increased in these samples and its median per-run ELD maximum was 183.45 → 225.73 ms; this is not presented as a tail-latency win. Candidate Bun CPU/reply ranged 500.06–540.66 ms versus baseline 496.77–522.17 ms. Node also varied: candidate first-delta p50 ranged 13.188–14.837 s versus baseline 14.181–14.468 s. No control was discarded for being slow. Bun ELD adds the documented 10 ms baseline to native excess timing; its histogram differs from Node's.

Across controls, Node completed 770 → 783 exact replies and Bun 780 → 778. All 12 control processes exited cleanly; candidate Bun's last close took 4.843 s on this unstacked base.

Remote Node 26.9 proof: `node scripts/check-changed.mjs` passed in **755.33 s wall**, with **zero lint/type warnings**. The three-file focused test command below passed **32 tests in 84.00 s wall**, including worker preparation; the new 100-client regression took **4 ms**.

The unstacked base still has slow shutdown: baseline Node burst was killed after 5.199 s; candidate Bun burst logged clean close at 4.835 s but remained alive at the harness's 5.147 s SIGKILL. Neither is counted as a clean process exit. These are retained limitations; the separate shutdown PR carries its own six-run-per-runtime before/after proof.

`pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed in **159.53 s wall**. This repository-owned lane builds the Gateway runtime, UI, metadata, and SDK boundary artifacts. Independent Codex autoreview is **scoped-clean through P2**, with no actionable findings. `git diff --check` passed.

Standalone changed-file cost: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/ws-connection/request-start.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **13 passed, 9.50 s wall** on local Node 26.10.0.

Focused local proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server/ws-connection/request-start.test.ts src/gateway/server/ws-connection/authenticated-request-dispatch.lifetime.test.ts src/gateway/server-request-entry.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **32 passed, 291.92 s wall** on the saturated host. Three tests failed as expected with the old owner (6.06 s wall); baseline owner suite passed 12 tests (38.96 s wall).

Paired source microbenchmark: 20 rounds per scenario, reversed A/B order, 200 main-thread CPU samples on local Node 26.10.0. A 100×5 setup burst changes **257 admitted/243 refused → 500/0**. One connection's 500 calls stays **257/243**. A 300×5 aggregate overload remains bounded at **1,025 admitted/475 refused**, including the active start. FIFO passed throughout. Equal-work queued-200 cost is **0.435 → 0.494 microseconds/request** (+0.060); quiet 1,000-start median CPU is **9.974 → 10.380 ms**, with substantial sample variation. There is no demonstrated CPU win.

Deslop completed without additional edits. Line delta: production **+34/−28 (net +6)**; tests **+27/−5 (net +22)**; docs **+3**. The small production increase adds ordinary per-connection accounting while removing the control-only counter path and quiet-start queue allocation.

Both baseline and candidate runtime builds emitted the same five inherited warnings: two experimental TypeScript API notices, browser externalization of `node:path` from unchanged media-core imports, and the startup CSS advisory threshold. The local worker build also emitted inherited module-directive warnings from unchanged `@mdx-js/mdx` and `hast-util-to-estree` dependencies. No dependency patch, suppression, or baseline exception was added.
